documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two-month check after starting acamprosate.

No alcohol since the end of October, by his account, and his sister (in the waiting room) backs that up. Finishing the intensive groups at the program this month, then weekly counseling. Taking acamprosate three times a day, misses the midday dose now and then. Some loose stools the first couple of weeks, gone now. Cravings 'a lot less.' Sleep still rough but better. PHQ-9 6, no SI. Still smoking a pack a day; says one thing at a time.

Exam: BP, pulse and weight as charted, weight steady. Alert, bright, no tremor. Anicteric. Abdomen soft, no ascites. No edema.

A/P
- Severe AUD, abstinent ~2.5 months on acamprosate plus program. Real progress, told him so. Continue 666 mg TID.
- Cirrhosis: CMP, CBC, GGT today. Hepatology later this month.
- MDD: improving with counseling; no medication.
- HTN controlled on amlodipine.
- Tobacco: not ready; revisit once sobriety is steadier.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Liver numbers improving
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Kevin. Your liver enzymes are the best I've seen them: AST 61 (it has sat in the 70s), ALT 45 (around 50 before), GGT 112 (around 150 before). That is your liver responding to not drinking. Blood counts and kidney tests normal. Keep going.

documents.title: Hepatology follow-up
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Outside hepatology group, visit 1/27/2026.

Interval: a third admission for delirium tremens in November 2025, after which he started acamprosate through his primary care physician and joined an outpatient addiction program. He reports complete abstinence since late October. No decompensating events.

Medications: acamprosate 666 mg three times daily, thiamine 100 mg, folic acid 1 mg, multivitamin, omeprazole 20 mg, amlodipine 5 mg. NKDA.
Exam: Anicteric, no asterixis, no ascites, no stigmata of decompensation.
Labs 1/13: AST 61, ALT 45, GGT 112; December ultrasound without focal lesion or ascites.

Assessment: Compensated alcohol-related cirrhosis, Child-Pugh A, now with sustained early abstinence and improving enzymes.
Plan: Continue abstinence and acamprosate. Surveillance ultrasound in June. Repeat variceal screening endoscopy in late 2026 or 2027 if he remains abstinent. Follow-up in 6 to 8 months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up.

Still not drinking - five and a half months. Weekly counseling at the program, and a peer support meeting on weekends. Acamprosate three times a day, no side effects now. Mood better, PHQ-9 5, no SI. Smoking unchanged at a pack a day; he asked what the options are and I went through them; he wants to wait until summer.

No jaundice, swelling, confusion or bleeding. Heartburn controlled.

Meds: acamprosate 666 mg TID, thiamine 100, folic acid 1, MVI, omeprazole 20, amlodipine 5. NKDA.

Exam: Vitals as charted - BP at goal, weight stable. Well-appearing. No tremor or asterixis. Sclerae anicteric. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no ascites. No edema.

A/P
1. Severe AUD, sustained abstinence on acamprosate with counseling. Continue.
2. Compensated alcoholic cirrhosis - CMP, CBC, INR, GGT, Mg today. Hepatology has the June ultrasound scheduled.
3. HTN - continue amlodipine 5.
4. MDD - improving, continue counseling.
5. GERD, thiamine deficiency - no change.
6. Tobacco - will revisit; he knows to message me when he's ready.
7. Lung CT and FIT due in the fall.
Follow-up in about 5 months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: April labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kevin, your labs keep moving the right way: AST 54, ALT 41, GGT 88, bilirubin 1.1, magnesium 1.9. Clotting and blood counts are normal. Nothing to change. Proud of you.

No ascites.
reports.conclusion: No focal hepatic lesion. No ascites. Stable cirrhotic appearance and normal spleen size.
